# Windows and messages

Registering a window class, creating windows, the message loop, painting and DPI.

<h2 id="window-procedure"><code>WindowProcedure</code></h2>

```rux
pub type WindowProcedure = func(*var opaque, uint32, uint, int) -> int
```

A window procedure: the function the system calls with each message for a window of a class.
Its arguments are the window, the message number and the two message parameters, and its result is the message's
answer, which [`DefWindowProcW`](/docs/api/windows/window#def-window-proc-w) supplies for every message the procedure does not handle itself. A Rux function of
this type is passed directly; it is called with the platform's C convention on the thread that owns the window.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L12)

<h2 id="point"><code>Point</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Point {
    pub x: int32;
    pub y: int32;
}
```

A point in pixels, the `POINT` most window calls take.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L16)

**Fields**

| Name | Type    | Description                                      |
| ---- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `x`  | `int32` | The horizontal coordinate, growing to the right. |
| `y`  | `int32` | The vertical coordinate, growing downward.       |

<h2 id="rect"><code>Rect</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Rect {
    pub left: int32;
    pub top: int32;
    pub right: int32;
    pub bottom: int32;
}
```

A rectangle in pixels, the `RECT` that window sizes and paint regions are given as.
The right and bottom edges are exclusive, so the width is `right - left` and the height `bottom - top`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L26)

**Fields**

| Name     | Type    | Description                               |
| -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `left`   | `int32` | The left edge.                            |
| `top`    | `int32` | The top edge.                             |
| `right`  | `int32` | The right edge, one past the last column. |
| `bottom` | `int32` | The bottom edge, one past the last row.   |

<h2 id="message"><code>Message</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Message {
    pub window: *var opaque;
    pub message: uint32;
    pub wParam: uint;
    pub lParam: int;
    pub time: uint32;
    pub point: Point;
    pub privateData: uint32;
}
```

The `MSG` that [`GetMessageW`](/docs/api/windows/window#get-message-w) fills in: one message taken from the calling thread's queue.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L39)

**Fields**

| Name          | Type          | Description                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `window`      | `*var opaque` | The window the message is for, or null for a message to the thread itself.       |
| `message`     | `uint32`      | The message number, such as [`WM_DESTROY`](/docs/api/windows/window#wm-destroy). |
| `wParam`      | `uint`        | The first message parameter, whose meaning depends on the message.               |
| `lParam`      | `int`         | The second message parameter, whose meaning depends on the message.              |
| `time`        | `uint32`      | When the message was posted, in milliseconds since the system started.           |
| `point`       | `Point`       | Where the cursor was when the message was posted, in screen coordinates.         |
| `privateData` | `uint32`      | Reserved for the system.                                                         |

<h2 id="window-class-ex"><code>WindowClassEx</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct WindowClassEx {
    pub size: uint32;
    pub style: uint32;
    pub windowProcedure: WindowProcedure;
    pub classExtra: int32;
    pub windowExtra: int32;
    pub instance: *var opaque;
    pub icon: *var opaque;
    pub cursor: *var opaque;
    pub background: *var opaque;
    pub menuName: *char16;
    pub className: *char16;
    pub smallIcon: *var opaque;
}
```

The `WNDCLASSEXW` that [`RegisterClassExW`](/docs/api/windows/window#register-class-ex-w) reads: what every window of a class shares.
The class name and menu name are read during registration only; the system keeps its own copies.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L59)

**Fields**

| Name              | Type              | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `size`            | `uint32`          | The structure's size in bytes, `sizeof(WindowClassEx)`.                                                                        |
| `style`           | `uint32`          | The class style bits, such as [`CS_HREDRAW`](/docs/api/windows/window#cs-hredraw), combined with `\|`.                         |
| `windowProcedure` | `WindowProcedure` | The function that answers the messages for every window of the class.                                                          |
| `classExtra`      | `int32`           | Extra bytes the system keeps per class, usually zero.                                                                          |
| `windowExtra`     | `int32`           | Extra bytes the system keeps per window, usually zero.                                                                         |
| `instance`        | `*var opaque`     | The module the procedure is in, from `GetModuleHandleW(null)` for the program itself.                                          |
| `icon`            | `*var opaque`     | The large icon, or null for the default.                                                                                       |
| `cursor`          | `*var opaque`     | The cursor shown over the window, or null to leave it to the procedure.                                                        |
| `background`      | `*var opaque`     | The brush the background is erased with, or a `COLOR_` index plus one cast to a pointer, or null.                              |
| `menuName`        | `*char16`         | The NUL-terminated UTF-16 menu resource name, or null for no menu.                                                             |
| `className`       | `*char16`         | The NUL-terminated UTF-16 class name that [`CreateWindowExW`](/docs/api/windows/window#create-window-ex-w) names the class by. |
| `smallIcon`       | `*var opaque`     | The small icon, or null to derive it from the large one.                                                                       |

<h2 id="paint-struct"><code>PaintStruct</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct PaintStruct {
    pub deviceContext: *var opaque;
    pub erase: bool32;
    pub paint: Rect;
    pub restore: bool32;
    pub includeUpdate: bool32;
    pub reserved: uint8[N];
}
```

The `PAINTSTRUCT` that [`BeginPaint`](/docs/api/windows/window#begin-paint) fills in and [`EndPaint`](/docs/api/windows/window#end-paint) reads back.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L88)

**Fields**

| Name            | Type          | Description                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deviceContext` | `*var opaque` | The device context to draw with until [`EndPaint`](/docs/api/windows/window#end-paint). |
| `erase`         | `bool32`      | Non-zero when the background still has to be erased.                                    |
| `paint`         | `Rect`        | The part of the window that needs painting, in client coordinates.                      |
| `restore`       | `bool32`      | Reserved for the system.                                                                |
| `includeUpdate` | `bool32`      | Reserved for the system.                                                                |
| `reserved`      | `uint8[N]`    | Reserved for the system.                                                                |

<h2 id="hwnd-message"><code>HWND_MESSAGE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const HWND_MESSAGE: uint64 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFD;
```

`HWND_MESSAGE`: the parent that makes a window message-only, never shown and never enumerated.
It is `-3` as a pointer, so it is cast at the call: `HWND_MESSAGE as *var opaque`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L254)

<h2 id="dpi-awareness-context-per-monitor-aware-v2"><code>DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2</code></h2>

```rux
pub const DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2: uint64 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFC;
```

`DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2`: the process draws for each monitor's own scale.
It is `-4` as a pointer, so it is cast at the call. Without it the system stretches the window's pixels on any
monitor scaled above 100%, which is what makes an old program's text blurry.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L261)

<h2 id="adjust-window-rect-ex-for-dpi"><code>AdjustWindowRectExForDpi</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func AdjustWindowRectExForDpi(
    rect: *var Rect,
    style: uint32,
    menu: bool32,
    exStyle: uint32,
    dpi: uint32
) -> bool32
```

Grows a client rectangle to the window rectangle that holds it, at a given DPI.
The result includes the title bar and borders the style adds, measured for that DPI rather than the system's.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-adjustwindowrectexfordpi](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-adjustwindowrectexfordpi)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L275)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type        | Description                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rect`    | `*var Rect` | the client rectangle on entry, and the window rectangle on return                                              |
| `style`   | `uint32`    | the window's `WS_` style                                                                                       |
| `menu`    | `bool32`    | non-zero when the window has a menu bar                                                                        |
| `exStyle` | `uint32`    | the window's extended style                                                                                    |
| `dpi`     | `uint32`    | the DPI to measure the frame at, usually from [`GetDpiForWindow`](/docs/api/windows/window#get-dpi-for-window) |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)

<h2 id="begin-paint"><code>BeginPaint</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func BeginPaint(
    window: *var opaque,
    paint: *var PaintStruct
) -> *var opaque
```

Prepares a window for painting and fills in what needs painting.
Called only in answer to [`WM_PAINT`](/docs/api/windows/window#wm-paint), and always paired with [`EndPaint`](/docs/api/windows/window#end-paint), which validates the region.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-beginpaint](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-beginpaint)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L284)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type               | Description                                         |
| -------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `window` | `*var opaque`      | the window being painted                            |
| `paint`  | `*var PaintStruct` | receives the device context and the region to paint |

**Returns**: the device context to draw with, or null when none is available

<h2 id="create-window-ex-w"><code>CreateWindowExW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func CreateWindowExW(
    exStyle: uint32,
    className: *char16,
    windowName: *char16,
    style: uint32,
    x: int32,
    y: int32,
    width: int32,
    height: int32,
    parent: *var opaque,
    menu: *var opaque,
    instance: *var opaque,
    parameter: *var opaque
) -> *var opaque
```

Creates a window of a registered class.
The procedure receives [`WM_CREATE`](/docs/api/windows/window#wm-create) before this call returns, so the window is already set up when it does.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-createwindowexw](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-createwindowexw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L303)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type          | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exStyle`    | `uint32`      | the extended style bits, usually zero                                                                                  |
| `className`  | `*char16`     | the NUL-terminated UTF-16 name of a registered class                                                                   |
| `windowName` | `*char16`     | the NUL-terminated UTF-16 title, or null                                                                               |
| `style`      | `uint32`      | the `WS_` style bits, combined with `\|`                                                                               |
| `x`          | `int32`       | the left edge, or [`CW_USEDEFAULT`](/docs/api/windows/window#cw-usedefault)                                            |
| `y`          | `int32`       | the top edge, or [`CW_USEDEFAULT`](/docs/api/windows/window#cw-usedefault)                                             |
| `width`      | `int32`       | the width, or [`CW_USEDEFAULT`](/docs/api/windows/window#cw-usedefault)                                                |
| `height`     | `int32`       | the height, or [`CW_USEDEFAULT`](/docs/api/windows/window#cw-usedefault)                                               |
| `parent`     | `*var opaque` | the parent or owner window, [`HWND_MESSAGE`](/docs/api/windows/window#hwnd-message) for a message-only window, or null |
| `menu`       | `*var opaque` | the menu, or for a child window its identifier, or null                                                                |
| `instance`   | `*var opaque` | the module the class was registered by                                                                                 |
| `parameter`  | `*var opaque` | a value passed through to [`WM_CREATE`](/docs/api/windows/window#wm-create), or null                                   |

**Returns**: the new window, or null on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)

<h2 id="def-window-proc-w"><code>DefWindowProcW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func DefWindowProcW(
    window: *var opaque,
    message: uint32,
    wParam: uint,
    lParam: int
) -> int
```

Answers a message the way the system does when a window procedure does not handle it.
A procedure passes every message it does not answer itself on to this call, unchanged, and returns its result.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-defwindowprocw](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-defwindowprocw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L327)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type          | Description                   |
| --------- | ------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `window`  | `*var opaque` | the window the message is for |
| `message` | `uint32`      | the message number            |
| `wParam`  | `uint`        | the first message parameter   |
| `lParam`  | `int`         | the second message parameter  |

**Returns**: the message's default answer

<h2 id="get-message-w"><code>GetMessageW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetMessageW(
    message: *var Message,
    window: *var opaque,
    filterMin: uint32,
    filterMax: uint32
) -> int32
```

Waits for the next message of the calling thread and takes it from the queue.
The result has three meanings, not two: positive for a message, zero for `WM_QUIT`, which ends the loop, and
-1 for an error with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error), which a loop testing only for non-zero would spin on.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-getmessagew](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-getmessagew)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Window.rux#L378)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type           | Description                                                             |
| ----------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `message`   | `*var Message` | receives the message                                                    |
| `window`    | `*var opaque`  | the window to take messages for, or null for every window of the thread |
| `filterMin` | `uint32`       | the lowest message number to take, or zero for no filter                |
| `filterMax` | `uint32`       | the highest message number to take, or zero for no filter               |

**Returns**: positive for a message, zero for `WM_QUIT`, or -1 on failure

| ---------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |

| `wParam`  | `uint`        | the first message parameter  |
| `lParam`  | `int`         | the second message parameter |

**Returns**: the procedure's answer
